issues.legal_issue: A contract for sale subject to prior official permission remains enforceable by specific performance when the vendor is obliged to seek that permission and the purchasers are ready and willing to perform.
material_facts: The parties made an agreement for sale requiring the vendor to obtain official permission for the transaction.
The vendor applied for permission but later withdrew the application.
The purchasers extended the time for obtaining permission and were found ready and willing to perform their part of the contract.
The vendor refused to perform, and time was found not to be of the essence of the contract.
issues.conclusion: The contract was complete and enforceable. The vendor had to apply for the required permission and, if it was granted, convey the property; if permission was refused, the purchasers were entitled to the damages decreed by the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: A requirement that the vendor obtain official permission does not make an otherwise completed contract inchoate. The court may enforce the contractual obligation by directing the vendor to apply for permission, leaving the decision whether to grant it to the competent authority. The obligation to apply was implied in the contract. The Court relied on Motilal v. Nanhelal (1930) L.R. 57 I.A. 333.

rule.if: appeal_from_specific_performance_decree and contract_requires_vendor_to_obtain_permission and vendor_withdrew_permission_application and purchasers_ready_and_willing and vendor_refused_performance and time_not_of_essence

predicates.appeal_from_specific_performance_decree: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a decree sought for specific performance of a contract.
predicates.contract_requires_vendor_to_obtain_permi: The contract requires the vendor to obtain official permission before the transaction can be completed.
predicates.vendor_withdrew_permission_application: The vendor withdrew an application made to obtain the required permission.
predicates.purchasers_ready_and_willing: The purchasers were ready and willing to perform their part of the contract.
predicates.vendor_refused_performance: The vendor refused to perform the vendor's contractual obligations.
predicates.time_not_of_essence: The court found that time was not of the essence of the contract.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns specific performance of a contract requiring the vendor to obtain permission, and the vendor withdrew the application despite the purchasers' readiness to perform, the vendor must apply and complete the sale if permission is granted, with damages available if permission is refused.

issues.legal_issue: A point not raised in the High Court and unsupported by pleaded facts cannot be raised for the first time in the Supreme Court.
material_facts: In the Supreme Court, the appellant sought to argue that specific performance should not be granted in the circumstances.
That point had not been specifically raised in the High Court, and the necessary facts had not been pleaded.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not allow the appellant to raise the point for the first time in the Supreme Court.
issues.legal_principle: A point not specifically raised in the High Court and for which the necessary facts were not pleaded should not be permitted to be raised for the first time in the Supreme Court.

predicates.appeal_to_supreme_court: The proceeding is an appeal before the Supreme Court.
predicates.issue_not_raised_in_high_court: The party did not specifically raise the issue in the High Court.
predicates.necessary_facts_not_pleaded: The pleadings did not set out the facts necessary to support the issue.

issues.definition: In a Supreme Court appeal, an issue is not entertained for the first time when it was not specifically raised in the High Court and the necessary supporting facts were not pleaded.
